**Member of Technical Staff - Applied Scientist I**  
**Formal Methods for AI Driven Software Development Life Cycle**  
  
San Francisco Bay Area | Bellevue, Washington | Hybrid |  
  
**About AIVista**  
  
NTT DATA AIVista, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of NTT DATA, is based in Silicon Valley. We develop AI products for enterprises operating in complex regulatory environments. We work with NTT DATA Inc., NTT DATA Japan, and NTT DOCOMO to deploy systems for NTT clients. Our clients combine AIVista's product AI expertise with NTT DATA's industry knowledge and systems-integration experience.  
  
**The Role**  
  
The Applied Scientist will develop methods that turn natural-language intent into structured, machine-checkable artifacts and use those artifacts to make AI-driven software development more verifiable, traceable, and reliable. You will work from policies, regulations, standard operating procedures, requirements, process descriptions, application programming interfaces, and code to construct formal specifications, rule ontologies, process ontologies, contracts, tests, and proofs with complete source traceability.  
  
The work addresses two distinct assurance problems. Validation asks whether a formal artifact faithfully captures authorized intent. Verification asks whether an implementation satisfies that artifact. You will build measurable validation methods for omissions and mistranslations, integrate independent checkers and proof systems, and carry the resulting evidence through the AI-driven software development life cycle. The objective is a practical development workflow in which models may propose requirements, designs, code, tests, or proofs, while deterministic checkers, versioned evidence, and human authority determine what is accepted.  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Develop autoformalization methods that translate policies, procedures, regulations, requirements, and process descriptions into typed rules, process models, contracts, and formal specifications.
* Design restricted domain-specific languages and formal semantics that domain experts and engineers can review together, with clause-level provenance and versioned change histories.
* Build validation stacks using controlled source language, concretization, counterexamples, back-translation, cross-representation consistency, independent dual translation, and expert adjudication.
* Create specification-mutation, non-vacuity, and seeded-defect benchmarks that measure detection rates for omissions, weakenings, exception errors, and mistranslations.
* Integrate satisfiability modulo theories solvers, model checkers, theorem provers, static analyzers, type systems, and property-based or fuzz testing into independent verification harnesses.
* Develop verifier-guided generation and repair methods for specifications, code, tests, invariants, proofs, and counterexamples while keeping the checker outside the generative model's trusted path.
* Apply formal methods across the AI-driven software development life cycle, from requirements and architecture through model-generated implementation, continuous integration, release evidence, monitoring, and change-impact analysis.
* Study composition at system scale, proof and specification maintenance under change, and methods for preserving evidence across tool, model, dependency, and compiler versions.
* Connect formal artifacts to AIVista's data, rule, action, and process ontologies so runtime decisions can be traced to governing sources, versions, evaluated values, and accepted checks.
* Define assurance claims with explicit scope, assumptions, trusted components, checker versions, and acceptance boundaries; prevent stronger claims than the evidence supports.
* Partner with product and engineering teams to transition successful methods into production authoring, verification, and AI-driven software development workflows.
* Lead publications, patents, open-source contributions, and research partnerships in formal methods, programming languages, software engineering, knowledge representation, and AI-driven software development.

* At least 5 years of experience in formal methods, software engineering research, artificial intelligence, or machine learning, with significant experience applying research in production environments.
* A proven record of impactful research demonstrated through publications, patents, open-source tools, formal artifacts, or shipped software products.
* Deep experience in at least two relevant areas: formal specification, program verification, model checking, theorem proving, static analysis, type systems, program synthesis, requirements engineering, or autoformalization.
* Hands-on experience building with at least one proof assistant, theorem prover, satisfiability solver, model checker, static analyzer, or verification-aware language.

We are building that platform: an agentic operating system that our portfolio companies run on. It is a problem set with real data, real multi-tenant requirements, and very few precedents to copy from.

Beacon has raised $750M+ from investors including General Catalyst, Lightspeed, D1 Capital, CPMG, and the family offices of the founders of Stripe, DoorDash, and Ramp.

Members of Technical Staff (MTS) build the platform that everything else at Beacon runs on. You will own a piece of it end-to-end: design, implementation, operations, and long-term technical direction. This is a Staff Engineer role in everything but name. We run flat.

We are hiring for two roles. The bar is the same; the specialty differs.

* **Product and platform engineering.** A senior engineer who builds agentic products and the platform underneath them: services, APIs, data access, and deploy infrastructure. Works directly with the people who use them.
* **AI infrastructure.** An engineer who builds the systems around models: serving, retrieval, evals, observability, fine-tuning, and deployment into secure and regulated environments.

Both seats ship to real businesses, fast. You take a problem from the first conversation with a user to a system in production, and measure success by whether people use it.

Fine-tune open-weight models on proprietary data where a general model falls short. Build the retrieval and governed data access that ground agents in real business data. Choose which model handles which job, with cost, latency, and quality as explicit trade-offs.

* **Ship to real businesses, fast.** Take a problem from the first user conversation to a system in production.
* **Prove quality with data.** No model or prompt change ships on vibes.

Fifth Dimension is the most prominent AI company in real estate in the world, bringing the magic of AI automation to document-heavy industries . Our AI workspace helps leading investment managers, owners, and operators across the US, UK, and APAC automate complex workflows, extract insights from critical documents, and make faster, smarter decisions.

We're hiring a Forward Deployed Strategist to own delivery on our most important US accounts. You'll work in a pod with a forward deployed engineer, an account manager and our sales team, and you'll make the calls that decide whether a pilot becomes a firm-wide deployment: which workflow comes first, who needs to be in the room, what we build and what we don't. Customers will trust you because you understand their business. Our product team will listen to you because you've seen what works.

**What a week looks like**
--------------------------

**Monday.** Pod reviews across your three US accounts. One is on track. One has an MD asking for a bespoke dashboard. One has gone quiet: asset management hasn't logged in for ten days. You move that one to the top of the week.

**Tuesday.** On site with the quiet account. You sit with two asset managers through quarter-end and find the step that eats a week a month: reconciling operator reports against the rent roll. By the afternoon you've built a first version in the product, on their own documents, and they've told you what it gets wrong.

**Wednesday.** You move the FDE's week onto that workflow and off the dashboard. Then you write to the MD: why the dashboard can wait, what the team gets instead, and when.

**Thursday.** Two hours with our CTO and the FDEs. Three accounts have asked for some version of the same reconciliation. You bring the brief: what's common, what's one customer's preference, and what the template should be.

**Friday.** Three asset managers ran this week's reconciliation in 5D, and nobody opened the spreadsheet. You post the weekly update for each pod: what moved, what's stuck, what you decided. Then you sit in on a sales call with a prospect who has the same problem, to hear how they describe it.

This is a forward-deployed week at Fifth Dimension. You decide what we build for our most important customers, and you make sure they use it. What works in one account becomes product for all of them.

**About Us**
------------

Fifth Dimension builds AI software for the firms that invest in and manage real assets. We help people work with complex documents and business data, from leases and financial models to investment memos. We're a Series A company with offices in London, New York and Singapore.

* AI-first. You build with AI yourself, and you can tell a customer exactly where it will and won't help.

**What This Role Is Not**
-------------------------

* A product manager role with a roadmap. You shape the product from the field; you don't own the backlog.
* An engineering role. You don't need to write production code; our FDEs do. You do need to build in the product and understand what's being built.
* Account management or customer success. Your pod has an account manager. You own the strategy, not the calendar.
* Sales. There's no quota. You'll sit in on sales calls to learn the market, not to close.

-----------------

A signed pilot is a bet, not a deployment. Real estate investment firms carry decades of process, documents in every format, and teams with good reason to be sceptical of AI. The first use case decides whether the rest of the firm follows.
